_about: Load measurements; scripts/load.py writes this file and renders docs/LOAD.md from it. local: N orders through the committed test builds in LiteSVM (compute units exact, cluster time derived). runs: what an operator measured on a cluster with a test issuer, newest last.

not_exercised.pay: knos_pay takes a token GitHub did not sign only in PayOrder on a PRIVATE order funded from a Balance, under a key the Balance's own wallet registered; that order is funded by FundOrderBalance, which takes GitHub's tokens only, one per order. A test issuer cannot fund and pay N orders, so PayOrder was not sent on the cluster; its compute units are measured in the local simulator.
not_exercised.fund from a Balance: FundOrderBalance and the faucet take GitHub's tokens only. The orders were funded by a wallet (FundOrderWallet), in a mint made for the run.

written_by_every_tx: the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the Balance's side account (one per funder)
the Balance's token account (one per funder)
the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the fee account (FEE_OWNER's token account of the mint) (one per mint, for every relayer and funder)
the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the relayer's token account, where its tip arrives (one per relayer)

latency.stage_split: not apart in these samples; scripts/latency_stages.py splits the payments whose relay log line carries the stage fields: docs/RELAY.md, "Where a token waits"

bounds.from: 29 requests a deliverable (23 reads and 6 writes counted); 1,000 an hour for a repository (GitHub)
bounds.lift: more repositories; GitHub Enterprise Cloud (15,000 an hour)

bounds.limit: the meter's statement, recomputed from the logs
bounds.scope: each buyer and seller, each month
bounds.from: `knos statement --meter` reads at most 100,000 transactions of a month's account, one RPC request each (src/knos/settle/v2/meter.py); a 30-day month, one evaluation a deliverable, one transaction an evaluation. Not a limit on the work: past it the month's account is still the count, and the recomputation from logs is cut short
bounds.lift: batching the meter: one RecordBatch token carries up to 100,000 evaluations under one Merkle root, so a month is a few transactions whatever its volume

bounds.from: 3 comments a deliverable (counted); 500 content-generating requests an hour (GitHub)
bounds.lift: more repositories

bounds.from: 2 jobs a deliverable (counted), each taken as busy for the p95 of merge-to-paid, 58 s (recorded, 40 samples; a job's own time on the runner was not measured apart); 20 jobs at once (GitHub)
bounds.lift: a larger plan (Pro 40, Team 60, Enterprise 500); self-hosted runners, which this limit does not count

bounds.from: 8.43 orders a second for one key that pays the fees (derived by scripts/load.py)
bounds.lift: a fee key per repository or per team (KNOS_RELAY_KEY is a repository secret)

bounds.limit: the fee account of the mint
bounds.from: 162.8 payments a second in one mint (derived by scripts/load.py)
bounds.lift: NEEDS A PROGRAM CHANGE: PayOrder writes FEE_OWNER's one token account of the mint. The change would be for PayOrder to take any of K fee accounts (a seed of the fee-owner authority and an index, the index chosen by the relayer), all swept to the same owner; nothing off chain can spread it

bounds.from: 205.5 fundings a second for one Balance (derived by scripts/load.py from measured compute units and 12M units an account a block)
bounds.lift: one Balance per team in place of one per organisation: a Balance's address is the owner's id, the wallet that opened it and the mint, and a funding comment spends the Balance that lists its commenter, so each team's wallet opens its own (`knos balance open`) and lists its own people. The hot account is split by configuration; every Balance keeps its own cap, and no order can take more than its Balance holds

bounds.from: 73 requests a deliverable (23 reads and 8 writes counted, 42 polls of the relay log at the p95 wait); 1,000 an hour for a repository (GitHub)
bounds.lift: the job's own relay (no polling); more repositories; GitHub Enterprise Cloud (15,000 an hour)

bounds.limit: the public relay's pass, one token at a time
bounds.scope: every customer of the public worker
bounds.from: 2 tokens a deliverable, carried one after another; a token taken as the median of merge-to-paid, 25 s (recorded; it includes the runner's start, so the relay's own share is smaller and one relayer carries at least this many)
bounds.lift: the job's own relay; or several relayers (anyone can run one: the chain takes each token once, whoever carries it)

bounds.from: 5 comments a deliverable (counted); 500 content-generating requests an hour (GitHub)
bounds.lift: more repositories; or the job's own relay, which posts no token comment
